label: Tipo Carora

names.text: Taken from the "Other names" line of the Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch. The article's page title is Carora cattle and it is headed Tipo Carora.

about.text: A dairy breed from the town of Carora in Lara state, western central Venezuela. It was developed from the early 1930s by crossing Brown Swiss bulls with local Criollo cows. It is kept for dairy production in tropical climates and is also used in crossbreeding with Holstein cows and with indicine breeds.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: location, dairy use in tropical climates, crossbreeding with Holstein and indicine breeds. The Frontiers article, read on WebFetch, gives the cross of Amarillo de Quebrada Arriba with Brown Swiss and the development about a century ago.

origin.place: The town of Carora, Lara state, western central Venezuela.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "Breeding began in the 1930s", so the formed range is 1930 to 1939. The Frontiers article describes the breed as developed "around a century ago", which fits. Location from both.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "In 2013, the registered population was 13,682 cows and 644 bulls." This is the cow count only. Not stated whether all are milked.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "In 1998, cows averaged 3180 kg of milk over a 305-day lactation." The article does not say where the data was collected, so no country is given.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "Milk protein averages about 3.7%". No year or place is given.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the breed is for dairy production in tropical climates. Its use as a sire for dual-purpose crosses with indicine breeds is not counted as a breed purpose here.

facts.v: About 90% of the cattle carry a slick, short, glossy coat from the slick hair gene. Bulls that do not carry it in two copies are culled based on their male offspring. The home region has monthly average temperatures of about 22 to 38 °C and humidity up to 90%.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch. The 90% figure and the temperature and humidity are as stated in the article, with no year given.

facts.v: Declared a Patrimonio Nacional in 1992, with a genetic improvement programme and herd-book set up at that time. The breeders' association started in 1979 and the Venezuelan government recognized the breed in 1982.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch, as stated in its history section.

facts.v: A 2025 pedigree study of the Carora Cattle Association records found low-average genetic diversity, rising inbreeding over time, and Brown Swiss genes increasing in the stock. The authors describe the breed as undergoing genetic diversity loss.

sources.text: Frontiers article, read on WebFetch: the abstract and conclusion. The Brown Swiss increase is from the Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch, which cites a pedigree study of 4,324 animals; the Frontiers article is the basis for the diversity and inbreeding statements.

gaps: Could not reach the FAO DAD-IS breed page, so no current risk status is given. Sources conflict: Wikipedia cites FAO (2007) listing the breed as extinct, which sits against the 2013 registered count and the 2025 study's large population. No fat, lactose or solids figures found. The 2025 pedigree counts (72,411 females, 8,067 males) are for pedigree records over several periods, not one year, so they are not used as a head count. A 1975 to 1986 average of 2433 kg in 244 days appears in a Wikipedia mirror, not on the article itself, and is left out.
